1.explanation:
All of these functions participate in discovering, loading and rendering language definitions in Prism. 

• getPeerDependentsMap and getPeerDependents in components/index.js calculate which other language modules must be reloaded when a given language changes. 

• loadLanguages in components/index.js is the central loader that `require()`s prism-<lang> files (e.g. prism-gcode.js) and hooks them into Prism.languages.

• buildContentsHeader in examples.js builds the HTML header for a language’s examples, referencing its alias and dependencies. To support ‘gcode’ you must add appropriate metadata so this function produces the correct headings and usage instructions.

• loadLanguage (examples.js) fetches the actual language script (via $u.script), and update (examples.js) triggers code highlighting on newly loaded examples. Both must be able to handle the new gcode identifier so that Prism.highlightElement is invoked on G-code snippets.
1.bug_scenario: The user wants Prism to support G-code (“gcode”) syntax highlighting. In the provided screenshot you can see typical G-code commands (e.g. “G1 X0 Y0 ; Home X and Y…”, “M109 S200 ; Heat hotend…”) rendered as plain text. The bug is that Prism does not yet recognize or highlight these G- and M-commands, nor the coordinate/property tokens (X, Y, Z, E, F, etc.), so adding a new Prism language definition (e.g. prism-gcode.js) and wiring it into Prism’s loader is required.

2.explanation: Prism’s architecture requires each language to have a component file named prism-<language>.js and be registered in the components metadata. The loadLanguages function in components/index.js is responsible for loading prism-<language>.js based on the language identifier; since “gcode” isn’t listed in components.languages, loadLanguages never requests prism-gcode.js. Similarly, the examples.js script iterates over components.languages to populate the Examples page and then calls loadLanguage(lang) for each enabled language; because gcode isn’t known, update() never highlights it. To fix the bug, you must: 1) Add a prism-gcode.js language definition (with comment, keyword and property patterns) alongside the other prism-<language>.js files. 2) Register gcode in the project’s components metadata so that components/index.js’s loadLanguages can discover and require prism-gcode.js. 3) Ensure examples.js sees gcode in components.languages and calls loadLanguage('gcode') so that highlightElement can apply the new syntax rules.
2.bug_scenario: The user is requesting that Prism add syntax highlighting support for G-code (the NC programming language used by CNC and 3D-printer firmware) under the language identifier “gcode.” In the screenshot we see lines such as “G1 X0 Y0 …” rendered with no special highlighting (just plain text), demonstrating that Prism currently does not know about or load any “prism-gcode.js” component. As a result, comments, G/M codes and coordinates are not colorized.
